test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 21 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The sum of the simple interest and the compound interest on ₹5,600 at the same rate of interest per annum for two years is ₹2,061.36, when in the case of compound interest, it is compounded annually. What is the rate of interest per annum?
solution:
Given:

A sum ₹ 5,600 gives ₹ 2,061.36 including both simple interest and compound interest on the sum at the same rate in 2 years.

Formula used:

Simple interest = (P × R × t)/100

Compound interest = P(1 + (R)/(100))t - P

Where P = principal

R = rate of interest

t = time

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest be r% per annum

Then, According to the Question, we get:

Compound interest + Simple interest = 2061.36

⇒{P(1 + (R)/(100))t - P} + (P × R × t)/100 = 2061.36

⇒ 2061.36 = (5600 × r × 2)/100 + {5600(1 + (r)/(100))² - 5600}

⇒ 5600 + 2061.36 = 112r + 5600{1 + (r²)/(10000) + (2r)/(100)}

⇒ 7661.36 = 112r + 5600 + 0.56r² + 112r

⇒ 7661.36 - 5600 = 224r + 0.56r²

⇒ 2061.36 = 0.56r² + 224r

⇒ 0.56r² + 224r - 2061.36 = 0

On dividing by 0.56 both sides, we get:

⇒ r² + 400r - 3681 = 0

⇒ r² + 409r - 9r - 3681 = 0

⇒ r(r + 409) - 9(r + 409) = 0

⇒ (r + 409)(r - 9) = 0

⇒ r = 9% as rate can't be negative so - 409 is not valid.

∴ The Required rate is 9%.
